 In The Court Of Sh. Jitendra Singh :
 Additional Sessions Judge (Electricity),

In The Matter Of:-
Cnr No. Dlnw01-011258-2023

Shri Mahesh Kashyap
Son of Late Shri Chhote Lal

Sector-11, Rohini, Delhi-110085.

 Judgment 
1. Vide this order, I shall dispose of the appeal filed under Section 29 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (hereinafter referred to as 'D.V. Act') against the judgment dated Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.1 of 18 24.07.2023 (hereinafter referred to as 'impugned judgment') passed by Ld. MM, Mahila Court-01, North-West, Rohini Courts, Delhi in CC no.450/4/2023 (New No.4999/2016), titled as Renu vs. Mahesh Kumar under Section 12 of the PWDV Act whereby the application filed by the respondent/ wife (hereinafter referred to as "complainant") under Sec. 12 of PWDV Act has been partly allowed against the appellant/husband (
hereinafter referred to as "respondent").
2. Notice of the appeal is issued to the complainant/wife and the she has entered her appearance,
TCR has been received and arguments have been heard. 
Allegations as contained in the application filed under Sec. 12 of D.V. Act :-

1 3. Brief facts of the case are that complainant got married to the respondent on 15.06.2009 as per Hindu Rites and Ceremonies with great pomp and show and out of the said wedlock one daughter was born. It is stated that it was the second marriage of the respondent but despite this fact, the father of the complainant had spent a huge amount beyond his capacity in the said marriage and provided all sorts of articles, jewellery etc. as per the demands. Soon after the marriage, respondent and his family members started harassing the complainant. That respondent/ husband was a habitual drunker and under the influence of alcohol he used to beat the complainant without any rhyme or reason and never contributed towards the household expenses and abused the complainant/wife in filthy language when she asked for the household expenses. It is further stated that on 27.07.2013, respondent/ husband came to the house of the complainant/ wife and forced her to come with Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.2 of 18 him. That thereafter, he gave something to the complainant to eat and the complainant became unconscious and the respondent went away with the child leaving the complainant at unknown place and after 15 days, the complainant came back to her parental house with the help of the police officials. Thereafter, the present complaint case was filed. 
4. DIR was filed. The respondent was summoned vide order dated 21.11.2013 and he put his appearance through his counsel on 04.06.2014. Respondent filed WS wherein he denied the factum of marriage and all the allegations levelled by complainant against him. 
5. During the course of proceedings, vide order dated 15.01.2018 respondent was proceeded ex-parte and matter was listed for ex-parte PE. 
During ex-parte PE, complainant tendered her evidence as Ex.CW1/A relied upon the documents Ex.CW1/A to Ex.CW1/E & Ex.CW1/G and the also the documents marked as Mark-A to Mark-C. Sh.
Jagbir Singh was examined as CW-2 and the complainant evidence was closed. 
Submissions by Ld. Counsel for the Appellant / Respondent:-
6. It is submitted by the ld. Counsel for the respondent that the findings of the Ld.
Trial Court are contrary to law and facts. It is further submitted that the finding of the ld. Trial Court that the respondent has successfully proved the existence of domestic relationship between herself and appellant is totally erroneous and perverse and therefore, an immediate interference is warranted. No cogent evidence has been brought on record by the complainant to prove that she is legally wedded wife of the respondent or that she resided together with the appellant in a Mahesh Kashyap vs.
Renu Page no.3 of 18 shared household. The complaint mentions that the marriage between the respondent and the complainant was solemnized on 15.06.2009 according to Hindu Rites and Customs however, she has failed to file any marriage photographs, marriage card or any other documentary evidence which establishes the solemnization of marriage between the respondent and complainant. As per Sec. 7(2)
of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, a marriage is deemed to be completed and binding when the rites and ceremonies include 'Saptapadi" are performed. 
Mahesh Kumar vs Renu on 18 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91092698/
2 7. The complaint dated 09.07.2013 filed at CAW Cell by the respondent is silent on the date of marriage but specifies the place of marriage as Haridwar and the names mentioned in the complaint are 'Renu' and Mahesh' only and they are not suffixed by the surname Kashyap. It is submitted that the Discharge Slip of Brahm Shakti Hospital (Ex.CW1/D) mentions the patients details as Mrs. Renu w/o Sh.
Mahesh. As per rules, it is the obligation of the hospital to convey the names of the parents with date of birth of the child as per their record but the said date of birth certificate shows a different picture and creates a grave suspicion about the manipulation of record. The respondent is already a married person since 24.05.1991 with Smt. Meera, d/o Sh. Sukhnandan Pardesi and that the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate the evidences such as the marriage card, few photographs of marriage of respondent with complainant, Aadhar card and voter card of the wife of the respondent which sufficiently establish the existence of marriage of the respondent with Smt. Meera. The wife of respondent is still alive and has been staying with the respondent ever since the date of marriage and in view of the subsistence of earlier marriage of the respondent, no valid Mahesh Kashyap vs.
Renu Page no.4 of 18 marriage could have taken place between the respondent and the complainant and therefore, the case of the complainant is completely false, baseless, concocted and without any substance. It is submitted that the complainant has failed to prove that she was in a domestic relationship with the respondent and that she was subjected to domestic violence by respondent. 
The Ld. Counsel has relied upon the following judgments:-
(i) Sneha Ahuja Vs. Satish Chander Ahuja and another, 2021 SCC OnLine Del 4984:
(2022) 1 RCR ( Civil) 234.
(ii) C.L. Jain Vs. Raghubir Singh, 2012 SCC OnLine Del 1556.
(iii) Dolly Rani Vs. Manish Kumar Chanchal, 2024 INSC 355.
(iv) Ram Sarup Gupta Vs. Bishun Narain Inter College, (1987) 2 SCC.
(v) National Textile Corporation Ltd. Vs. Nareshkumar Badrikumar Jagad, (2011) 12 SCC 695.
It is prayed that the present appeal may be allowed. Submissions on behalf of the Complainant /
wife :-
8. It is submitted that the impugned judgment does not suffer from any infirmity and the present appeal has been filed by the respondent just to create undue pressure on the complainant/wife. It is further submitted that the respondent is a habitual drunkard and in drunken state, he used to beat the complainant and used abusive language against her. It is stated that the complainant never discharged his obligations as a husband and father towards the complainant and her child. It is further submitted that the respondent beaten up the complainant blue and black and against the same respondent filed a complaint before the CAW Cell, Sector-3, Rohini Mahesh Kumar vs Renu on 18 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91092698/
3 dated 09.07.2013. The Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.5 of 18 complainant has always compromised and faced all atrocities of the respondent to save her matrimonial life but the respondent never showed any love, affection and interest with the complainant. It is submitted that the present appeal is wrong, false,
fabricated, baseless and frivolous and the same is not legally maintainable and sustainable in eyes of law. The Ld. Counsel has relied upon the following judgments:-
(i) Muddasani Venkata Narsaiah (D) The. Lrs. Versus Muddasani Saojan. 
(ii) Lingeswaran Etc. Versus Thirunagalingam. 
(iii) Union of India Versus National Project Construction Corp. Ltd.
(iv) M/s. Gautam Associates Versus Food Corporation of India.
(v) Chanmuniyat(s) Versus Virendra Kumar Singh Kushwaha & Anr.
(vi) Badshah Versus Sou. Urmila Badshah Godse & Anr.
(vii) Shhailesh Bopche Versus Anita Bapche.
( viii ) Harvinder Kaur @ Arvinder Kuar Versus Gurdeep Singh. 
(ix) Prabha Tyagi Versus Kamlesh Devi. 
Accordingly, it is prayed that the appeal may be dismissed.
9. Detailed arguments have been heard. Certain judgments have been filed on behalf of the parties and same have now been duly considered. 
The Position in Law:-
LEGAL FRAMEWORK 10. The Provision of the D.V. Act which are relevant for the disposal of the present appeal are extracted as under :
"2. Definitions.--In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,--
(a) 'aggrieved person' means any woman who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the respondent and who alleges Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.6 of 18 to have been subjected to any act of domestic violence by the respondent;
Mahesh Kumar vs Renu on 18 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91092698/
4 (f) 'domestic relationship' means a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage,
adoption or are family members living together as a joint family;
(s) 'shared household' means a household where the person aggrieved lives or at any stage has lived in a domestic relationship either singly or along with the respondent and includes such a house hold whether owned or tenanted either jointly by the aggrieved person and the respondent, or owned or tenanted by either of them in respect of which either the aggrieved person or the respondent or both jointly or singly have any right, title, interest or equity and includes such a household which may belong to the joint family of which the respondent is a member, irrespective of whether the respondent or the aggrieved person has any right, title or interest in the shared household. 
3. Definition of domestic violence --For the purposes of this Act, any act, omission or commission or conduct of the respondent shall constitute domestic violence in case it-- (a) harms or injures or endangers the health, safety, life, limb or well-being, whether mental or physical, of the aggrieved person or tends to do so and includes causing physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse and economic abuse; or (b) harasses, harms, injures or endangers the aggrieved person with a view to coerce her or any other person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any dowry or other property or valuable security; or (c) has the effect of threatening the aggrieved person or any person related to her by any conduct mentioned in clause (a) or clause (b); or (d) otherwise injures or causes harm, whether physical or mental, to the aggrieved person.
Explanation I.--For the purposes of this section,--
(i) 'physical abuse' means any act or conduct which is of such a nature as to cause bodily pain, harm, or danger to life, limb, or health or impair the health or development of the aggrieved person and includes assault, criminal intimidation and criminal force;
(ii) 'sexual abuse' includes any conduct of a sexual nature that Mahesh Kashyap vs.
Renu Page no.7 of 18 abuses, humiliates, degrades or otherwise violates the dignity of woman;
(iii) 'verbal and emotional abuse' includes- Mahesh Kumar vs Renu on 18 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91092698/
5 (a) insults, ridicule, humiliation, name calling and insults or ridicule specially with regard to not having a child or a male child; and (b) repeated threats to cause physical pain to any person in whom the aggrieved person is interested;
(iv) 'economic abuse' includes-- (a) deprivation of all or any economic or financial resources to which the aggrieved person is entitled under any law or custom whether payable under an order of a court or otherwise or which the aggrieved person requires out of necessity including, but not limited to, house hold necessities for the aggrieved person and her children, if any, Stridhana, property, jointly or separately owned by the aggrieved person,
payment of rental related to the shared house hold and maintenance;
(b) disposal of household effects, any alienation of assets whether movable or immovable, valuables, shares, securities, bonds and the like or other property in which the aggrieved person has an interest or is entitled to use by virtue of the domestic relationship or which may be reasonably required by the aggrieved person or her children or her Stridhana or any other property jointly or separately held by the aggrieved person; and (c) prohibition or restriction to continued access to resources or facilities which the aggrieved person is entitled to use or enjoy by virtue of the domestic relationship including access to the shared household.
Explanation II.--For the purpose of determining whether any act, omission, commission or conduct of the respondent constitutes 'domestic violence' under this section, the overall facts and circumstances of the case shall be taken into consideration.
12. Application to Magistrate--(1) An aggrieved person or a Protection Officer or any other person on behalf of the aggrieved person may present an application to the Magistrate seeking one or more reliefs under this Act: Provided that before passing any order on such application, the Magistrate shall take into consideration any Domestic Incident Report received by him from the Protection Officer or the service provider. (2) The relief sought for under Sub-Section (1) may include a relief for issuance of an order for payment of compensation or damages without prejudice to the right of such person to institute a suit for compensation or damages for the injuries Mahesh Kashyap vs.
Renu Page no.8 of 18 caused by the acts of domestic violence committed by the respondent:
Provided that where a decree for any amount as compensation or damages has been passed by any court in favour of the aggrieved person, the amount, if any, paid or payable in pursuance of the order made by the Magistrate under this Act shall be set off against the amount payable under such decree and the decree shall,
notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908),
or any other law for the time being in force, be executable for the balance amount, if any, left after such set off.
Mahesh Kumar vs Renu on 18 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91092698/
6 (3) Every application under Sub-Section (1) shall be in such form and contain such particulars as may be prescribed or as nearly as possible thereto. 
(4) The Magistrate shall fix the first date of hearing, which shall not ordinarily be beyond three days from the date of receipt of the application by the court. 
(5) The Magistrate shall Endeavour to dispose of every application made under Sub-Section (1) within a period of sixty days from the date of its first hearing...". 
11. After analyzing the relevant provisions of the D.V. Act, it is culled out that the complainant can get relief under the said Act only when she qualifies to be a aggrieved person. The expression "aggrieved person" means a woman who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the respondent and has been subjected to any act of domestic violence by the respondent. The expression "domestic relationship"
means a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time,
lived together in a shared household. The relationship may be by : (i) consanguinity,
(ii) marriage or, (iii) through a relationship in the nature of a marriage, (iv) adoption or, (v) are family members living together as a joint family. The expression "domestic relationship" is a comprehensive as well as expansive one. If aggrieved person is living or at any point of time lived together in "shared household" with the person against whom allegations of domestic violence have been made, the Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.9 of 18 provisions of D.V. Act would apply. It is relevant to note the expression "marriage" also encompasses "relationship in the nature of marriage".
12. For seeking relief under the D.V. Act, in the case of relationship in the nature of marriage, the pre condition is that the allegation of domestic violence must relate to the period of subsistence of relationship in the nature of marriage. 
Findings:-
13. From the pleadings and the documents, it is the case of the complainant that she got married with the respondent who is resident of H.No.D 1/31-32, Block-D, PKT-1, Sec. 11, Rohini, Delhi on 15.06.2009 at Haridwar. The complainant and the respondent started residing at B- 55, Mange Ram Park, Budh Vihar, Phase-I, Delhi-86. A girl child was borne out of the said wedlock on 18.12.2010. 
As the complainant was subjected to domestic violence she left the shared household and shifted to her parental home. 
14. It is the defence of the respondent that the complainant is not his wife and he does not have any relationship with the complainant. Moreover, the respondent has denied the paternity of the child allegedly borne out of the wedlock between the complainant and the respondent. The respondent has even denied that he lived in the shared household with the respondent. 
Name & identity of the Respondent :- 
Mahesh Kumar vs Renu on 18 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91092698/
7 15. It is vehementally argued that the name of the respondent has been different in the documents relied by the complainant which implies that the complainant is not even aware about the correct name of the respondent though, she has alleged that the respondent has lived with Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.10 of 18 her in a shared household. It is pertinent to mention here that the respondent himself has filed documents wherein his name has been reflected as 'Mahesh Kumar Kashyap', 'Mahesh Kashyap' and 'Mahesh'. Record reveals that an application for dismissal of the case was moved by the respondent on 20.04.2017 before the Trial Court, in the affidavit attached with the said application, the name of the respondent has been mentioned as 'Mahesh Kumar Kashyap'. Similarly, in the affidavit filed with the written statement, the respondent has mentioned his name as 'Mahesh Kumar Kashyap'. During the trial, the respondent has moved an exemption application wherein the medical prescription shows his name as 'Mahesh Kashyap'. Moreover, the copy of the wedding card which was filed along with the application for dismissal, the respondent's name has been mentioned as 'Mahesh'. This clearly shows that the respondent himself is using his name in different nomenclature. Therefore, this court has no hesitation to hold that the respondent 'Mahesh Kashyap' is the same person who has been referred as 'Mahesh' and 'Mahesh Kumar Kashyap' in the documents relied by the respondent. 
Domestic Violence:-
16. In order to prove that the complaint was subjected to domestic violence, she has examined herself as CW-1 and has relied upon evidence by way of affidavit which is Ex. CW-1/1. The complainant has distinctly mentioned that she was subjected to physical beatings and mental torture by the respondent. The relevant extract of her evidence by way of affidavit Ex.CW1/1 is given as under :
"....4. That the deponent deposes that the respondent is a Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.11 of 18 habitual drunkard, due to drunkenness, the respondent beats the deponent and uses the abusive language against thee deponent and further caused utmost mental and physical cruelties, torture and harassment to the deponent. The respondent has never discharged his obligation of a devoted husband and father towards the deponent and her child and he did not even look after, maintain. 
5. That the deponent deposes that the deponent was forced and compelled to do the entire household work but without any appreciation and deponent was threatened that in case they did not act as per their directions respondent would kill her. The respondent treated the deponent with utmost cruelty and physical assault again and again. 
6. That the deponent deposes that the regular beatings, mental and physical torture and harassment by the accused persons/respondent resulted into weakens of the health of deponent but even then none had taken pity upon the deponent, rather with the passage of time the torture and misconduct of the respondent became more sharpened, aggressive and violent. The deponent became pale and weak and fearing for her life and future and marital life as all her dreams was shattered after seeing the Mahesh Kumar vs Renu on 18 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91092698/
8 said act and misconduct of the respondent.
8. That the deponent deposes that the that on 27.07.2013 the respondent came in the parental home at that time no body present at home expect the deponent and her child. The respondent pressurized to the deponent to bring with him same time and for the sake of her matrimonial life the deponent went to the respondent but the respondent offered to eatable things after that the deponent unconscious and the respondent with her child went away and left the deponent unknown place and after 15 days the deponent came to parental home with the help of Police persons of the P.S. Mandwali. 
12. That the deponent deposes that the regular beatings, mental and physical torture and harassment by the accused resulted into weakening of the health of the deponent, but even then none had taken pity upon the deponent, rather with the passage of time the torture and misconduct of the respondent became more sharpened, aggressive and violent. The deponent became pale and weak and fearing for her life and future and marital life as all her dreams were shattered after seeing the said act and misconduct of the respondent. ....". 
Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.12 of 18 17. The registration of the complaint dated 27.08.2013 (Mark- C) before the CAW Cell has been admitted by the respondent in his written statement. Therefore, Mark-C can be read in evidence. The allegations of domestic violence stands corroborated by the said complaint. It is pertinent to mention here that the respondent has failed to cross-examine the complainant (CW-1) and has even not lead any evidence in support of his defence. Therefore, the testimony of the complainant has remained uncontested and unrebutted. The complainant has successfully proved on record that she was subjected to domestic violence. 
Shared Household:- 
18. It is contended by the respondent that the complainant has failed to mention the address of the premises in which allegedly the complainant and respondent lived together which implies that the complainant and the respondent never had a shared household. The documents relied by the complainant precisely shows that the parties lived together at H.No. B-55, Mange Ram Park, Delhi. The argument of the respondent does not have any weight as the documents are to be read with the petition. Even if, the complainant has failed to mention the address where they lived together in her application it will not act as a hurdle for seeking the relief under the D.V. Act as in complaint Mark-C the address has been distinctly mentioned.
Domestic Relationship:-
Mahesh Kumar vs Renu on 18 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91092698/
9 19. The question arises whether the complainant was in a domestic relationship with the appellant ? The intention of the parties and the nature of living including the nature of household have to be Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.13 of 18 looked into to find out as to whether the parties intended to treat the premises as shared household or not. The intention of the parties has to be gathered from the pleadings as find mentioned in the petition wherein complainant has stated that the respondent never discharged the obligation of a husband and father. Moreover, to prove that the complainant has lived with respondent in a shared household, she examined her landlord Sh. Jagbir Singh as CW2 who has categorically mentioned in his evidence by way of affidavit that the complainant and the respondent resided in his premises from 14.05.2010 to 02.03.2011 as husband and wife. During the subsistence of tenancy, a female child was born on 18.12.2010 in Braham Shakti Hospital, Budh Vihar. The relevant extract of the examination in chief of CW-2 is reproduced as under:-
"... 1. That the deponent is permanent residence of above mention address and owner of this house. 
2. That the deponent deposes that the address of my is correct i.e. B-55, Mange Ram Park, Budh Vihar, Phase-1, Delhi-86. 
3. That the deponent deposes that the Renu and Mahesh has resided in my above mention house as a tenant as husband and wife from 14.05.2010 to 02.03.2011. 
4. That the deponent deposes that during tenancy one female child was born on 18.12.2010 of Renu and Mahesh in Bhram Shakti hospital, Budh Vihar, Delhi.....". 
The relationship by way of marriage or Relationship in the nature of marriage :-
20. The factum of marriage has been categorically denied by the respondent. The D.V. Act has to be interpreted in a manner to effectuate the very purpose and object of the Act. For seeking relief under the D.V. Act, the complainant can not be expected to strictly prove all the ingredients of marriage. Any other interpretation would defeat the Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.14 of 18 purpose of the Act. The complainant has brought on record the Birth Certificate of her minor daughter as Ex.CW1/G wherein the name of the father has been mentioned as 'Mahesh Kashyap' and the address has been mentioned as B-55, Mange Ram Park, Delhi. This is the same address on which the complainant has alleged that they lived as husband and wife. 
Even otherwise, the complainant can seek relief under the D.V. Act if she is able to establish that the relationship between the complainant and the respondent was in the nature of marriage.
21. The relationship in the nature of marriage has been explained by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as Prabha Tyagi vs. Kamlesh Devi, Crl. Appeal Mahesh Kumar vs Renu on 18 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91092698/
10 No.511 of 2022, D.O.D. May 12, 2022. The relevant extract is reproduced below for ready reference : 
".....It would be useful to refer to the following judgments of this Court which have been taken into consideration relationship in the nature of marriage :
(a) In D. Velu Samy v. D. Patchaiammal - [(2010) 10 SCC 469], this Court discussed the concept of "relationship in the nature of marriage" in the context of the DV Act,
and it was held to be akin to a common law marriage. It was held that the parties must have lived together in a 'shared household' as defined in Section 2(s) of the DV Act. It was opined that not all live-in relationships would amount to a relationship in the nature of marriage to get the benefit of D.V. Act, but only to such relationships,
which qualify as common law marriages. 
The requirements prescribed under law in order for a relationship to be recognized as a common law marriage were adumbrated as follows:
(i) The couple must hold themselves out to society as being akin to spouses;
(ii) They must be of legal age to marry;
(iii) They must be otherwise qualified to enter into a legal marriage;
(iv) They must have voluntarily cohabited and held themselves Mahesh Kashyap vs.
Renu Page no.15 of 18 out to the world as being akin to spouses for a significant period of time (b) In Indra Sarma v. V.K.V. Sarma - [(2013) 15 SCC 755], the question as to whether disruption of a live-in relationship by failure to maintain a woman involved in such a relationship amounted to "domestic violence" within the meaning of Section 3 of the D.V. Act, was considered. It was held that entering into a marriage either under the Hindu Marriage Act or Special Marriage Act or any other personal law applicable to the parties, is entering into a relationship of public significance, since marriage, being a social institution, many rights and liabilities flow out of that relationship. Thus, the concept of marriage gives rise to civil rights. This Court referred to the following guidelines, which would determine whether a relationship between persons was in the nature of marriage, to ultimately hold that the DV Act had been enacted to cover a couple who had a relationship in the nature of marriage, so as to provide a remedy in Civil Law for protection of women in relationships, which are in the nature of marriage as per paragraph 56 which is extracted as under :
"56. We may, on the basis of above discussion cull out some guidelines for testing under what circumstances, a live-in relationship will fall within the expression "relationship in the nature of marriage" under Section 2(f) of the D.V. Act. The Mahesh Kumar vs Renu on 18 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91092698/ 
11 guidelines, of course, are not exhaustive, but will definitely give some insight to such relationship :
56.1. Duration of period of relationship. - Section 2(f) of the D.V. Act has used the expression "at any point of time", which means a reasonable period of time to maintain and continue a relationship which may vary from case to case, depending upon the fact situation. 
56.2. Shared household.- The expression has been defined under Section 2(s) of the D.V. Act and, hence, needs no further elaboration. 
56.3. Pooling of resources and financial arrangements.- Supporting each other, or any one of them, financially, sharing bank accounts, acquiring immovable properties in joint names or in the name of the woman, long-term investments in business,
shares in separate and joint names, so as to have a long-standing relationship, may be a guiding factor. 56.4. Domestic arrangements.- Entrusting the responsibility,
especially on the woman to run the home, do the household activities like cleaning,
cooking, maintaining or upkeeping the house, etc., is an indication of a relationship in the nature of Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.16 of 18 marriage. 
56.5. Sexual relationship.- Marriage-like relationship refers to sexual relationship,
not just for pleasure, but for emotional and intimate relationship, for procreation of children, so as to give emotional support, companionship and also material affection,
caring, etc. 56.6. Children.- Having children is a strong indication of a relationship in the nature of marriage. 
The parties, therefore, intend to have a long-standing relationship. Sharing the responsibility for bringing up and supporting them is also a strong indication. 
56.7. Socialisation in public.- Holding out to the public and socialising with friends,
relations and others, as if they are husband and wife is a strong circumstance to hold the relationship is in the nature of marriage. 
56.8. Intention and conduct of the parties.- Common intention of the parties as to what their relationship is to be and to involve, and as to their respective roles and responsibilities, primarily determines the nature of that relationship...". 
22. The complainant has proved on record that a girl child was born out of the wedlock between complainant and respondent on 18.12.2010. This fact is a strong indication that they had a intimate relationship for procreation of children. As per the testimony of CW-2, the complainant and the respondent lived as a husband and wife in the share household from 14.05.2010 to 02.03.2011. The intention and conduct of the parties clearly suggest that the relationship was in the nature of marriage. The uncontested and unrebutted testimony of CW-1 and CW-2 is sufficient to prove on record that the complainant and respondent was in a domestic relationship and the complainant Mahesh Kumar vs Renu on 18 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91092698/
12 was subjected to domestic violence in the period of subsistence of relationship in the nature of marriage.
23. In view of the above discussion, this Court is of the opinion that the impugned order does not suffers from any infirmity. 
Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.17 of 18 Accordingly, the instant appeal stands dismissed. File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
